Typeface

The same sentence twice: first in var(--font-family-base), then in that stack with Public Sans Web removed. If the two rows look identical, Public Sans Web is NOT loading and this page — and the app — is rendering in the fallback. The face IS self-hosted, so identical rows now mean a Resource is missing or misnamed on the app — not that nobody shipped it.

Font weight

400 and 700 are the design's own weights. 500 is a brand-owner decision (Kharlo Ridado, 2026-08-25, PR #9), not a value from the ref — it exists so OutSystems UI's --font-semi-bold has a step to land on. A weight only renders as drawn if a real face is loaded for it — all three below are shipped as separate Resources. Three visibly distinct rows mean all three landed; two rows that look alike mean one face is missing and the browser is synthesising or snapping to its neighbour.

Line height

Unitless ratios, as the design states them — a unitless line-height inherits as a ratio and re-computes per element, so a child at a different size stays proportional. Shown across several wrapped lines, because that is the only place a ratio is visible.

--line-height-base 1.62

Federal agencies deliver services the public depends on. Clear typography is how that information becomes usable — line length, size and rhythm decide whether a page can be read at all, long before anyone reaches its content.
